jobs.title: Business Development Manager, Distributed Energy
jobs.excerpt: Role SummaryThe Business Development Manager, Distributed Energy, is responsible for accelerating Fluke’s penetration and market share across the rapidly expanding EV charging infrastructure and solar/energy-storage ecosystems.
jobs.description:
Role Summary

The Business Development Manager, Distributed Energy, is responsible for accelerating Fluke’s penetration and market share across the rapidly expanding EV charging infrastructure and solar/energy-storage ecosystems. This role blends strategic market development with hands-on selling to unlock new logo wins, drive product-line expansion, secure multi-site contracts, and influence standards and specifications that preference Fluke test and measurement tools.

The role spans the full distributed energy value chain: EV charge point operators (CPOs) and network providers, EVSE installers and electrical contractors, fleet electrification programs, solar EPCs, O&M providers, utility-scale solar and storage owner-operators, commissioning agents, and utilities interconnecting distributed energy resources. A strong understanding of EVSE installation and maintenance workflows, PV system commissioning and O&M, energy storage, and electrical safety practices is essential.

Key Responsibilities

Market Expansion & Business Development

  • Build and execute a strategic growth plan to expand Fluke’s presence across EV charging (public DCFC networks, fleet depots, workplace/retail L2) and solar (utility-scale, C&I, and distributed PV plus storage).
  • Identify and convert new logo opportunities across CPOs, EVSE manufacturers and installers, fleet operators, solar EPCs, O&M providers, asset owners, commissioning agents, and utilities supporting DER interconnection.
  • Develop multi-year growth strategies for key distributed energy customers and map executive stakeholders and influencers to secure enterprise-wide adoption, specification preference, and expansion opportunities.
  • Develop standardized Fluke-preferred workflows and playbooks for EVSE commissioning and maintenance technicians, PV installers, O&M field teams, and electrical contractors.
  • Drive adoption of Fluke solutions across installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and electrical safety workflows.
  • Analyze competitive solutions and market dynamics to develop strategies that position Fluke as the preferred test and measurement provider across distributed energy workflows.

Pipeline Creation & Conversion

  • Establish and execute a 12–24-month pipeline focused on critical product categories including EV charging station analyzers, solar irradiance and I-V curve tracing tools, insulation testers, CAT III 1500 V solar instruments, power quality analyzers, thermal imaging, battery analyzers, and digital multimeters.
  • Generate early-stage funnel through proactive outreach to CPOs, EVSE installers, solar EPCs, O&M providers, and utility DER programs.
  • Drive demand through vertical events, industry associations (e.g., RE+, SEIA, CharIN, EVSE/NECA forums), and strategic channel activation.
  • Co-sell with field sellers and channel partners to progress high-value deals through close.
  • Own revenue growth, pipeline development, and market-share expansion objectives for the distributed energy segment, with accountability for converting strategic opportunities into scalable, multi-site customer relationships.

Contracts, Standards, and Specifications

  • Influence standards and specifications at CPOs, EPCs, asset owners, and utilities to require Fluke tools across EVSE commissioning, PV acceptance testing (IEC 62446), storage, and electrical safety workflows.
  • Secure multi-site and multi-year agreements that consolidate spend and reduce TCO for network operators, EPCs, and O&M providers.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with Marketing and Product Management to identify key distributed energy customer personas, define their operational workflows and pain points, and translate those insights into targeted messaging, solution positioning, and market development strategies.
  • Partner with Marketing to develop verticalized content, case studies, and campaigns tailored to EV charging and solar audiences.
  • Provide VOC to Product Management to inform roadmap prioritization for EVSE, PV, and energy-storage test needs.
  • Support Sales Enablement in building segment-specific training for field sellers, distributors, and contractor-focused teams.

Thought Leadership & Vertical Expertise

  • Serve as Fluke’s subject matter expert across the distributed energy ecosystem including EV charging networks, fleet electrification, solar EPC/O&M, and energy storage.
  • Articulate Fluke's value proposition around productivity, reliability, safety, regulatory compliance, and total cost of ownership during executive-level customer engagements and industry forums.
  • Represent Fluke at conferences, commissioning groups, contractor forums, and technical associations tied to e-mobility and renewable energy.
  • Educate internal teams on emerging trends such as NEVI/state charging programs, high-power charging, megawatt charging for fleets, solar-plus-storage growth, interconnection constraints, and evolving codes and standards (NEC, UL, IEC).

Qualifications

  • 8–12+ years of experience in business development, strategic sales, or key account management within distributed energy, EV infrastructure, solar, energy storage, electrical infrastructure, test & measurement, or related technical industries.
  • Demonstrated success driving new logo acquisition, account expansion, and multi-site or multi-year agreements in complex B2B environments.
  • Strong understanding of distributed energy ecosystems, including EV charging infrastructure, solar generation, energy storage, utilities, fleet electrification, and contractor networks.
  • Working knowledge of EVSE installation and maintenance workflows, PV commissioning processes, energy storage systems, electrical safety practices, and applicable industry codes and standards.
  • Experience engaging with and selling to charge point operators (CPOs), EVSE manufacturers and installers, solar EPCs, O&M providers, utilities, fleet operators, asset owners, commissioning agents, or related stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to build and execute strategic account plans, map stakeholders, and influence decision-makers at multiple organizational levels, including executive leadership.
  • Experience developing and managing 12–24 month pipelines, including early-stage opportunity creation and funnel development.
  • Ability to articulate value propositions tied to reliability, safety, productivity, regulatory compliance, and total cost of ownership (TCO).
  • Track record of cross-functional collaboration with sales, marketing, product management, and channel partners to drive revenue outcomes.
  • Strong executive communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.
  • Experience selling through and with distribution channel partners.
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% across North America.
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

  • Direct experience in EV charging infrastructure, solar construction and commissioning, energy storage systems, distributed energy resources (DERs), or electrical infrastructure environments.
  • Background selling or supporting test and measurement equipment, power quality tools, thermal imaging, electrical safety instrumentation, battery analysis, or related technologies.
  • Experience influencing standards, specifications, or approved vendor lists within large operators, EPCs, utilities, fleet organizations, or asset owners.
  • Familiarity with distributed energy technologies and emerging trends, including high-power EV charging, fleet electrification, solar-plus-storage systems, DER interconnection, and grid modernization initiatives.
  • Experience working with or selling through channel partners, distributors, contractor networks, or utility ecosystems.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop vertical-specific workflows, playbooks, or standardized solutions.
  • Knowledge of industry standards and regulatory frameworks impacting EV charging, solar, energy storage, electrical safety, and compliance.
  • Experience participating in or presenting at industry associations, technical forums, standards organizations, or conferences.
  • Ability to analyze competitive landscapes and develop displacement strategies.
  • Master of Business Administration (MBA) or advanced degree preferred.

Fortive Corporation Overview

Fortive's essential technology makes the world safer and more productive. We accelerate transformation in high-impact fields like workplace safety, build environments, and healthcare.

We are a global industrial technology innovator with a startup spirit. Our forward-looking companies lead the way in healthcare sterilization, industrial safety, predictive maintenance, and other mission-critical solutions. The AmpSeq Programme Director is responsible for leading the cross-functional programme required to scale AmpSeq from strategic growth priority into a robust, governed, commercially reliable and operationally sustainable global platform.

The role provides overall programme leadership across customer intake, design, pilot execution, kit manufacture, services delivery, BioIT, quality, supply chain, commercial readiness, product development and site implementation. It is accountable for governance, prioritisation, risk management, stakeholder alignment, KPI tracking and delivery of the AmpSeq roadmap across Middleton, Berlin and other contributing sites. The role works closely with Operations, Commercial, Innovation Hub, Product Development, Quality, Bioinformatics, Supply Chain, Finance, PMO and senior leadership to ensure AmpSeq growth is delivered with clear ownership, scalable processes and measurable business impact.

 

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to capably perform each of the following essential duties:

  • Business Impact: Lead the AmpSeq programme as a strategic growth platform, driving delivery of revenue, customer conversion, operational scale-up, service readiness and programme outcomes across global stakeholders.

  • Innovation & Change: Direct cross-functional change across NGS workflows, portal adoption, panel design, pilot execution, manufacturing scale-up, BioIT support, quality controls and customer onboarding.

  • Type of Work: Balance strategic programme leadership with operational issue resolution, ensuring near-term delivery risks are managed while building a sustainable future-state operating model.

  • Key Stakeholders: Partner with global Operations, Commercial, Product Development, Innovation Hub, BioIT, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, PMO, site leadership and senior executives to align priorities and unblock delivery.

  • Communications: Provide clear programme updates, escalation packs, decision logs, risk summaries, KPI reporting and leadership communications for operational reviews, steering committees and executive forums.

  • People Management: Lead through direct and matrixed teams, setting expectations, assigning accountable owners, clarifying decision rights and supporting capability development across programme workstreams.

  • Process Oversight: Own the programme governance model, including operational huddles, Tier 2 escalation reviews, steering committee decisions, intake and questionnaire review, action tracking, decision tracking and risk management.

  • Subject Matter Expertise: Apply strong understanding of NGS services, AmpSeq customer workflows, design-to-pilot processes, kit manufacture, service delivery, BioIT dependencies, quality expectations and operational scale-up.

  • Continuous Improvement: Identify and drive improvements in turnaround time, first-time-right performance, traceability, inventory management, workflow standardisation, dashboarding and operational handoffs.

  • Data & Metrics: Establish and manage KPIs for revenue progression, opportunity conversion, panel design performance, pilot status, turnaround time, manufacturing readiness, capacity, quality and customer delivery.

  • Physical Demands: Primarily office, meeting and virtual work, with periodic site visits to laboratory, manufacturing and service environments.

  • Policy & Standards Compliance: Ensure programme activities comply with LGC policies, quality expectations, EHS requirements, customer commitments, data controls and relevant operational standards.

  • Other Duties As Assigned: Perform other duties as required to support AmpSeq growth, business continuity and strategic delivery priorities.

Essential Knowledge and Qualifications:

  • Degree or equivalent experience in life sciences, molecular biology, genomics, biotechnology, operations, programme management or a related discipline.

  • Significant experience leading complex cross-functional programmes in life sciences, genomics, laboratory services, manufacturing, operations or commercial delivery environments.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage strategic programmes with multiple workstreams, dependencies, risks, stakeholders and senior leadership governance requirements.

  • Strong understanding of operational scale-up, customer onboarding, service delivery, supply chain dependencies, quality requirements and process governance.

  • Experience using dashboards, action logs, decision logs, risk registers and KPI reporting to drive accountability and programme delivery.

  • Strong communication skills, including ability to simplify complex operational and technical issues for executive, commercial, technical and site-based audiences.

Desired Knowledge and Qualifications:

  • Experience with NGS, AmpSeq, KASP, FlexSeq or comparable high-throughput genotyping service platforms.

  • Experience working across multiple global sites and managing delivery through matrixed teams.

  • Formal project or programme management qualification, such as PMP, PRINCE2, Lean, Six Sigma or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience with ERP, LIMS, Salesforce, Tableau, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project or other operational planning and reporting tools.

  • Familiarity with customer-facing technical programmes, product launch readiness, validation, manufacturing readiness and service implementation.

What we offer (US based-employees):

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits for employees and dependents

LGC strongly believes that every job applicant and employee should be valued for their individual talents regardless of age, disability, race, color, ethnic or national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, religion, or belief. Short listing, interviewing and selection will always be carried out without regard to gender, sexual orientation, marital status, color, race, nationality, ethnic or national origins, religion or belief, age, or trade union membership.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

This position requires current U.S. work authorization. We are unable to sponsor or assume sponsorship for temporary visas (including H‑1B, H‑2B, OPT, O‑1, TN)

LGC is a leading, global life science tools company, providing mission-critical components and solutions into high-growth application areas across the human healthcare and applied market segments. Our high-quality product portfolio is comprised of mission-critical tools for genomic analysis and for quality assurance applications, which are typically embedded and recurring within our customers’ products and workflows and are valued for their performance, quality and range.

Our tools play a key role in customer workflows from discovery applications through to commercial manufacture and enable its customers to: bring new diagnostics and therapies to market; progress research and development; optimize food production; and continuously monitor and enhance the quality of food, the environment and consumer products.

LGC’s 175+ years of scientific heritage, combined with a track record of innovation and value-enhancing acquisitions, has enabled the company to build its product portfolio and expertise, and develop deep relationships with customers, industry partners and the global scientific community. Join us and help us achieve our mission of Science for a Safer World!

Our kit and component manufacturing sites are situated across the US (Middleton, Petaluma, and Novato) and Europe (Berlin and Lystrup) and are underpinned by either ISO 13485 or ISO 9001 compliance. These capabilities support a wide portfolio of off-the-shelf components and kits critical to NGS workflows including magnetic beads, oligos, enzymes, and library prep kits. Additionally, our primary manufacturing capabilities enable customization and bulk (OEM) manufacture of reagents such as key NGS enzymes for high volume applications.

This is a remote position.

Customer Service Specialist – Make a Difference for Our Customers Every Day

Position Overview:

We are looking for energetic individuals who have an interest in providing our clients' customers with excellent customer service support from your secure home office. We aim to delight every customer every day. As a Customer Service Specialist, you’ll play a key role in helping customers achieve their goals, whether it’s finding the perfect product, resolving an issue, or ensuring a smooth order process. You’ll use your empathy, resourcefulness, and problem-solving skills to deliver exceptional service that leaves a lasting impression. If you thrive on making customers successful and are motivated to turn challenges into wins, we’d love to hear from you.

XACT@Home is only available in AL, FL, GA, ME, MD, MS, NC, PA, VA, UT, and TX. Please check back later for availability in your state.

What You’ll Do:

  • Be a trusted resource for customers, assisting them via phone, email, and live chat with product selection, order questions, and everything in between
  • Use active listening and genuine curiosity to understand customers’ needs and challenges, and then recommend solutions that exceed expectations
  • Approach customer interactions with a "How can I make this easy for the customer?" mindset, removing the burden of extra work from the customer and inspiring confidence
  • Communicate clearly with other departments to ensure timely order processing and delivery
  • Meet established performance metrics and continually set goals for professional growth
  • Maintain accurate and detailed records of customer interactions to keep things streamlined and efficient
  • Identify opportunities to enhance the customer experience through thoughtful upselling, cross-selling, or problem-solving
  • Stay informed with company updates so you can offer the best guidance to our customers ● Contribute to projects and other tasks as needed to support company growth

Who You Are:

  • Someone who truly gets excited about making customers happy through understanding and solving their problems
  • A problem-solver who is motivated to find solutions and create positive outcomes
  • A great communicator who can connect, empathize, and build trust with customers
  • A great listener who can connect with customers and understand their needs
  • Organized and detail-oriented, ensuring every customer’s request is handled effectively
  • Energetic, adaptable, and excited to learn and grow in a fast-paced environment

What You Bring:

  • High school diploma or equivalent; some college coursework is a plus
  • Prior customer service experience is ideal, but we’re happy to train the right candidate
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and decision-making skills
  • A proactive, positive attitude with a focus on solutions and customer satisfaction
  • Ability to multitask and prioritize in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable using technology and troubleshooting technical issues.
  • Ability to type at a minimum 40 WPM

Requirements

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to remain in a stationary position for prolonged periods while working at a computer
  • Ability to communicate effectively with customers over the phone
  • Must be able to perform repetitive tasks, such as typing, with attention to detail

Technical Requirements:

  • High-speed DSL or cable connection, rated at least 10 MB download speed and 2 MB upload speed.
  • Dedicated home office space, which is free from distraction, and with a door that can be closed and locked. We will ask you to provide a picture of this space. Your workspace must be a dedicated working environment that is used exclusively by you.
  • A personal desktop computer running a licensed version of Windows 10 or higher (Windows 11 preferred), with 8 GB of RAM (Core i3 processor, or better). Laptops are not eligible for the work-at-home agent program.
  • A 19″ flat panel monitor (minimum), multiple displays recommended and preferred.
  • A wired network connection (wireless is not permitted) ● A webcam, for training, compliance, and collaboration purposes.
  • An approved-brand USB headset for VOIP (Plantronics, Logitech, Jabra, Sennheiser, Surf Onn, Discover, Microsoft LifeChat Series).
  • A modern mobile phone (iOS or Android) that can be used for multi-factor authentication purposes. Must have iOS 17 or greater, or Android OS 12 or greater. Apple or Samsung brand preferred.

Benefits

Everyone needs time to relax and enjoy life — and at XACT, we’re firm believers in work-life balance. Our paid time off (PTO) program allows team members to earn time they can use to unwind and enjoy life outside of work.

Although we’re open 24 hours a day, we believe in flexible scheduling that integrates work into your life — not the other way around. Set schedules, split shifts, and on-demand shift availability are just a few of the options we offer.

Full-time team members are eligible to join our company group plan through Aetna, once eligibility requirements are met.

Smile confidently!

XACT offers dental insurance through Sun Life to eligible team members. With both low- and high-benefit plan options, you’ll find one that fits your needs and makes you grin.

We see you, too!

We proudly offer VSP vision insurance to eligible team members. With strong coverage and savings on glasses and contacts, it's easy to see the value.

In addition to standard insurance options, we also provide supplemental products through Allstate — including accident, disability, and other coverage choices.

Relax — it’s expected.

We’re happy to provide safe, comfortable working environments designed with your well-being in mind. Our call centers feature employee lounges, quiet spaces, and cozy places to work.

We’re just one big family here, so pull up a seat and join in. As a team member — not an independent contractor — you can count on us for support. Whether you’re working in our contact centers or from your home office, we’ll equip you with the tools, technology, and 24×7 support you need to succeed.

Full-time Assistant Professor or Associate Professor, or Professor of Practice & Academic Program Director (APD) in B.S. Cybersecurity

Hybrid - San Diego, CA

National University is a veteran-founded, San Diego-based nonprofit. Since 1971, our mission has been to provide accessible higher education to adult learners. Today, we educate a student body from across the U.S. and around the globe, with more than 230,000 alumni worldwide. Our three schools and three colleges offer more than 200 accredited and licensed graduate and undergraduate programs. National University holds accreditation through the Western Senior College and Universities Commission (WSCUC).

Position Summary

The Department of Cybersecurity and Technology at National University invites applications for a Full-time Assistant or Associate Professor, Professor of Practice and Academic Program Director in B.S. Cybersecurity . Rank is commensurate with qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated record of, or potential for excellence in, teaching and scholarship in their field and a commitment to serving the University’s adult student body. This position works closely with other faculty within the discipline and administration contributing to programmatic strategies that ensure program quality, student engagement, and success. We are especially looking for a candidate who can contribute to the development and enhancement of our cybersecurity curriculum ensuring it meets the latest industry standards and addresses emerging threats. The ideal candidate should have hands-on knowledge of Linux, Windows, and a variety of cybersecurity tools.

The Academic Program Director (APD) is a full-time faculty member who directs the strategy, operations, and support for the degree program for which this role is responsible. As the primary spokesperson for all program (part-time and full-time) faculty and students, the APD will act as the primary source of information about specific programmatic strategies, needs and daily operations, and initiate and approve changes to ensure program quality, driving student engagement, and success. The APD serves as the lead discipline expert for the program as well as primary contact for multiple stakeholders. This position collaborates with program faculty in support of student success as well as the Director of Assessment to conduct program assessment on a regular basis to ensure the program is meeting the needs of the student and the program’s related industries, and where applicable, the programmatic accreditation requirements. This position ensures the incorporation of identified trends or changes into the curriculum, in collaboration with the Director of Curriculum and serves in either a direct or consulting role during course development, updating, and maintenance. The APD meets regularly with the College leadership (Department Chair/Associate Dean and/or Dean) to ensure that the program aligns with University and College goals and priorities.

In lieu of scholarship requirements, if you are selected as the candidate, you may be considered for a Professor of Practice position.

This position is remote. For San Diego-based candidates, the position is hybrid and meets with students twice/monthly for 2.5 hours each session.

Essential Functions

Candidates will be evaluated for their proficiency and potential in teaching, scholarship, and service. The main expectations of this position include:

Teaching

  • Teach and develop online and/or onsite courses in cybersecurity.
  • Maintain andragogical and subject matter expertise in the instructor’s field.
  • Create a positive learning environment for diverse learners.
  • Ensure course and program practices align with compliance and accreditation standards.
  • Adhere to the National University’s academic integrity policy.

Scholarship

  • Maintain a productive scholarship agenda suitable to a teaching university.
  • Engage in scholarly activities to maintain professional growth and accreditation expectations.
  • Participate in professional development as outlined in faculty policies.

Service

  • Participate in curriculum oversight, shared governance, and the student experience.
  • Serve on the university committees and engage in community activities that promote program outreach and university goals.
  • Participate in program meetings and advisory boards to integrate best practices and strategic initiatives.
  • Create, modify, and update BS Cybersecurity course material.

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications:

Education & Experience

  • Master’s degree in Cybersecurity or a related discipline required to qualify for the Professor of Practice rank.
  • Terminal degree in Cybersecurity or a related discipline required to qualify for Assistant Professor and Associate Professor ranks.
  • A minimum of 5 years of full-time faculty experience in higher education is required to qualify for the Associate Professor rank.
  • A minimum of 10 years of professional experience, evidence of significant professional achievement, and a minimum of 3 years of teaching/training experience required to qualify for the Professor of Practice rank.
  • At least 2+ years of industry experience in cybersecurity required.
  • Industry certifications such as: CISSP, SANS GIAC, CEH, CISM, CISA required.
  • Leadership or program management experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience with the National Security Agency Centers of Academic Excellence programs preferred.
  • Active involvement in the cybersecurity community preferred.

Required special conditions of employment include:

  • Background check.
  • Travel at least once annually to attend the annual Commencement ceremony (if held onsite).
  • Travel to attend cybersecurity-related events (typically 3-5 events/annually).

This position will be posted until filled.

For full consideration, interested candidates should provide the following:

  • A cover letter that includes a list of industry-related certifications, teaching experience, and industry experience.
  • A curriculum vita
  • Statement of teaching experience online and/or onsite

Candidate receiving offers will be offered a salary/pay rate commensurate with experience that vary based on a candidate’s qualifications, skills, and competencies. Absent exceptional circumstances, candidates will be offered a salary within this range for this position. jobs.excerpt: Job Description:POLITICO is seeking an aggressive, enterprising reporter to cover how the tech industry is shaping the new political landscape.
jobs.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an aggressive, enterprising reporter to cover how the tech industry is shaping the new political landscape. You will focus on how leading companies and executives are positioning themselves with the White House, Congress and regulators across America; which policies they’re advancing or fighting; who they’re lobbying and how Silicon Valley is preparing for the 2028 presidential campaign.


The beat will cover the companies at the center of the tech and AI industries — including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia and xAI — as well as the executives, founders, investors, lobbyists and political operatives driving the industry’s relationship with Washington and the states.


A deep source network among the biggest tech players in Silicon Valley and Washington will be essential. Those sources will drive breaking news on the tech industry’s political strategy, lobbying campaigns, corporate relationships and policy priorities, along with distinctive reporting on the personalities behind the industry’s growing political clout.


The beat will focus closely on who has the ear of President Trump, which executives are gaining access to the White House, who is building relationships on Capitol Hill, which tech leaders are becoming political players and how rivalries, alliances and personal relationships are influencing the industry’s political approach.


The policy portfolio will include artificial intelligence, antitrust and competition, data privacy, copyright, content moderation, online platforms, cryptocurrency, semiconductors, export controls, data centers and the tech workforce. The job will involve explaining the policy fights that matter most to Silicon Valley and, crucially, how the industry is seeking to influence them — through lobbying, political organizing, coalition-building and direct engagement with policymakers.


The beat will also explore the competing visions within Silicon Valley over AI policy, the growing influence of AI companies and investors, and the battles over regulation that could define the industry’s future. Following the money and political capital will be a key piece of the job: which companies are spending to influence policy, which lobbyists and advisers are gaining influence, what trade groups are prioritizing, which executives are becoming donors and advisers and how companies are positioning themselves on the biggest political and policy questions.


The reporter will dive in on how presidential candidates are courting Silicon Valley, which tech executives and investors are choosing sides, what the industry wants from the next administration and how tech executives are working to influence the candidates who could ultimately set tech policy.

The job will require someone who can move comfortably between Silicon Valley and Washington — someone who understands the tech industry on its own terms but can also recognize the political stakes behind its biggest decisions.


Breaking news, cultivating high-level sources and producing ambitious enterprise will be central to the role, with a focus on explaining how Silicon Valley is positioning itself, building influence and trying to determine what comes next.


The position will work closely with POLITICO’s teams to connect developments in Silicon Valley with policy and political battles in Washington, Brussels and other tech and political centers around the world.


What You’ll Need

  • Significant reporting experience covering tech, politics, policy and government.
  • A demonstrated ability to break news and deliver incisive, original reporting.
  • A deep understanding of the tech industry and the political and regulatory forces shaping it.
  • An established network of sources among tech executives, founders, investors, policymakers, lobbyists, lawyers and political operatives — or the ability to build one quickly.
  • Experience covering companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Nvidia, xAI or other leading tech companies is highly valued.
  • A track record of developing sources who can provide proprietary information about corporate strategy, executive relationships, lobbying efforts and political activity.
  • A strong interest in the personalities, relationships and power dynamics shaping Silicon Valley and Washington.
  • The ability to identify and cultivate sources among executives, lobbyists and political figures defining the tech industry’s relationship with government.
  • The ability to write clearly, accurately and efficiently on deadline.
  • The ability to juggle fast-moving breaking news with ambitious enterprise and investigative reporting.
  • Smart, innovative story ideas and a relentless drive to be first on consequential stories.
  • The ability to explain complex tech, political and policy developments clearly for an influential audience.
  • A collaborative spirit and willingness to work with reporters and editors across POLITICO’s California, Washington and global tech teams.
  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, accurate and nonpartisan journalism.

The anticipated salary range is $145,000–$160,000 per year. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO.

Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here. We hope to see your application soon!


About Us.

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital.


Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes.


Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist.


Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself.


These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization.


POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy. The company’s guiding principles - first articulated as The Essentials by founder Axel Springer in the aftermath of World War II - remain a cornerstone of the company’s foundation today. Learn more about Axel Springer.

Lead Backup & Recovery Engineer


As a Lead Backup & Recovery Engineer, you will coordinate activities related to the enterprise data protection architecture for on-premises and cloud environments. You will set the technical direction for how the organization protects and recovers its data. You'll define backup policies, recovery objectives, and data lifecycle strategy in agreement with the business, establish the governance framework and standards the estate is held to, and own recoverability assurance. You'll own platform strategy and vendor selection end to end, and lead backup platform migrations including sequencing, risk position, and cutover authority.


This is a technical leadership role rather than a day-to-day break-fix role; routine monitoring and first-line remediation sit with the operations team, while you own the architecture, standards, automation strategy, and final technical escalation above it. You'll present findings, risk positions, and program status to senior leadership, IT steering committees, and audit and risk functions, and defend architecture decisions under scrutiny. You'll set the capability development plan for engineers and operators and review the designs the team produces, while remaining hands-on enough to prototype new capability and lead the highest-risk implementation work personally.

Location: This role is approved to be fully remote and can be based anywhere in the United States.


Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Own the enterprise data protection strategy and architecture across on-premises, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments.
  • Define and maintain backup, retention, recovery, and data lifecycle standards, including RPO/RTO objectives aligned to business requirements.
  • Design and implement resilient, ransomware-resistant backup and recovery solutions using immutable, air-gapped, and isolated recovery capabilities.
  • Establish standard protection patterns for virtual, physical, database, containerized, SaaS, and cloud-native workloads.
  • Lead evaluation, selection, implementation, migration, and lifecycle management of enterprise backup and recovery platforms.
  • Develop disaster recovery architectures, replication strategies, failover/failback processes, and recovery testing programs that support business continuity objectives.
  • Serve as the technical authority during disaster recovery exercises, audits, major incidents, and recovery events.
  • Partner with Infrastructure, Cloud, Security, Storage, Database, and Application teams to ensure data protection requirements are incorporated into solution designs.
  • Define governance, compliance, and security controls supporting regulatory requirements such as SOX, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and internal security standards.
  • Own resource planning, performance management, growth forecasting, licensing strategy, and cost optimization for backup and recovery environments.
  • Establish reporting, dashboards, indicators, and service level metrics to communicate protection coverage, recovery readiness, risk exposure, and operational performance.
  • Drive automation initiatives to improve scalability, consistency, and operational efficiency across the backup estate.
  • Lead vendor relationships, product roadmap discussions, proof-of-concept evaluations, and technology recommendations.
  • Provide technical leadership, mentoring, design reviews, and escalation support for backup and recovery engineering teams.
  • Maintain hands-on technical involvement in architecture validation, complex problem solving, platform upgrades, and critical implementations.

Qualifications and Requirements:

  • 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience with enterprise backup and recovery platforms, including time in a lead, principal, or architect capacity.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, or a combination of education and experience.
  • Demonstrable experience leading enterprise-scale end-to-end migrations of backup systems, with accountability for cutover and validation.
  • Proven ownership of data protection architecture across a large, heterogeneous estate.
  • Experience establishing governance frameworks, standards, and SLA reporting where none previously existed.
  • Experience leading vendor selection, including RFP and RFI development, PoC evaluation, and formal recommendation.
  • Good background in requirements gathering, gap analysis, and formal solution documentation.
  • Deep understanding of cloud backup and cloud storage tiering in at least one major provider (AWS, Azure, OCI, or GCP), including object storage, archive tiers, lifecycle policies, and egress and cost implications.
  • Working knowledge of storage technologies including SAN, NAS, object storage, snapshots, and replication.
  • Deep understanding of disaster recovery frameworks, RTO and RPO design, and DR testing methodologies.
  • Experience designing immutable, ransomware-resilient, and air-gapped or isolated recovery architectures.
  • Familiarity with ITIL practices and formal change management processes.
  • Ability to communicate technical risk, options, and recommendations to upper management and steering committees, and to defend architecture decisions under scrutiny.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with multiple enterprise backup and recovery platforms, including complex or post-acquisition environments.
  • Experience developing and presenting data protection strategies within regulated industries.
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise database protection and application-consistent recovery (Oracle, SQL Server, SAP, PostgreSQL).
  • Experience protecting Kubernetes, containerized, cloud-native, and SaaS workloads, including Microsoft 365.
  • Proficiency with scripting, automation, and infrastructure-as-code methodologies.
  • Experience supporting budgeting, licensing strategy, vendor negotiations, and cost optimization initiatives.
  • Demonstrable ability to drive continuous improvement, service modernization, and operational excellence.

Preferred Certifications:

  • Vendor certifications in enterprise backup and recovery platforms.

  • Intercompany Matrix Management: Maintain a comprehensive register of all intercompany transactions to ensure complete, accurate, and timely monthly eliminations.
  • Reporting & Financial Statements: Prepare lender reporting packages, compliance covenant schedules, Group US GAAP financial statements, footnote disclosure packages, and annual financial disclosure checklists.
  • International Trial Balance Oversight: Review trial balance submissions for key international entities (South Africa, Mexico, Brazil), ensuring proper mapping to the group chart of accounts and maintaining data integrity.
  • Audit & Controls Support: Collect internal control evidence, track management letter recommendations, and coordinate audit request deliverables.
  • Equity Compensation: Oversee share-based compensation schedules, valuation tracking, and cost allocations across entities.
  • Treasury & Statutory Backup: Provide backup support for daily cash positioning and liquidity forecasting; assist the Statutory Reporting Manager during peak reporting cycles.

Requirements

Essentially, to ensure you succeed in this role you're going to need:

  • 4+ years of hands-on accounting experience with proven expertise in multi-entity group consolidations.
  • Recognized professional accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, CPA, or equivalent).
  • Strong practical knowledge of US GAAP, including foreign currency translation and intercompany eliminations.
  • Advanced Excel proficiency and comfort managing large, complex datasets.
  • Resilience, problem-solving mindset, and strong interest in software/AI automation.
  • Proficiency in spoken and written English, essential for daily communication across international markets and external partners.

It will also help you to have:

  • Big 4 or top-tier audit background with deep expertise in full-cycle financial reporting (statements, footnotes, control schedules), intercompany recharges, and cost-plus transfer pricing.
  • Hands-on experience leading or configuring new ERP and consolidation system implementations within a fast-paced, high-growth startup environment.
  • Proven track record of managing distributed financial operations, including external bookkeeping providers and regional accounting partners.

Benefits

  • We're proudly distributed across the globe, with each market being remote-first. Depending on which market you're joining, you might have office access or be fully remote - either works. All we ask is that you're based in the country/region this role is advertised in.

Technical Director (Perm, UK, Remote)

This is a permanent full time remote opportunity for those based in the UK.

About NearformNearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.

Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart.

As part of our Delivery Management function, you will help our clients build solutions and platforms, launch new product ventures, and fundamentally change how they operate.

You will work as part of a highly skilled, multidisciplinary team, typically consisting of designers, developers, DevOps engineers, and members of the client team.

Whether you’re a Delivery Manager, Technical Lead, or Technical Director, you will act as the bridge between client needs and timelines, ensuring the delivery of innovative, scalable solutions.

About the Technical Director role

As a Technical Director at Nearform, you will provide strategic and technical leadership across multiple projects, ensuring alignment with business goals while fostering innovation and excellence. Your role will involve technical vision-setting, client engagement, and team leadership to drive both project success and long-term growth.

  • Technical Strategy & Leadership – Define and communicate a clear technical vision, ensuring best practices in architecture, software development, and emerging technologies. Act as the final authority in critical design and delivery decisions.
  • Client Engagement & Advisory – Serve as a trusted advisor to CIOs, CTOs, and senior stakeholders. Lead discovery workshops, translate business objectives into technical strategies, and develop tailored solution proposals.
  • Project Execution & Delivery – Oversee technical execution, ensuring quality, scalability, and maintainability. Monitor project health, identify risks, and ensure successful outcomes through proactive leadership.
  • Team Leadership & Talent Development – Work with resourcing teams to ensure the right talent is staffed on projects. Foster a culture of excellence, mentorship, and innovation across teams.
  • Financial & Operational Oversight – Manage project burn-down, optimize resource allocation, and identify revenue growth opportunities while maintaining financial accountability.
  • Industry Influence & Thought Leadership – Stay ahead of industry trends, contribute to open-source projects, and engage in public speaking, blog writing, and mentorship. Champion Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) and sustainability initiatives within Nearform.

What we are looking for in this person

  • 15+ years of technical leadership experience, ideally within consulting, SaaS, or large-scale digital transformation projects.
  • Deep expertise in software architecture, cloud platforms, and modern development practices.
  • A strong track record of guiding technical decisions on complex, high-impact projects.
  • Experience leading pre-sales, discovery, and solution design discussions.
  • Strong ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • A consultative mindset, able to align business needs with technical strategies.
  • Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills to influence at all levels.
  • Hands-on experience with AI, databases, distributed systems, and modern software engineering best practices.
  • Experience leading and mentoring senior software development teams
  • A passion for continuous learning, innovation, and professional excellence.

Preferred Skills

  • Previous experience working in a fully remote, globally distributed environment.
  • Background in financial oversight of technology projects.
  • Experience contributing to open-source projects or technical thought leadership.
  • Prior exposure to AI-driven solutions and emerging technologies.

Benefits & Perks

  • Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance.
  • Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem!
  • Paid Time Off Package - We offer an annual leave of 25 days plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more.
  • Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in GBP) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join.
  • Training and Development Allowance - Nearform is committed to supporting and investing in employees’ ongoing learning and professional development. You will be encouraged to pursue relevant learning opportunities that support your growth and the growth of others, subject to manager approval.
  • Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team.
  • Pension & Insurances - We offer a pension match of up to 5% and Income Protection and Death in Service for peace of mind.

Our Interview Process

Talent Call (30 mins, Zoom)An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Team to learn more about your background, experience, and career goals. We'll also provide a high-level overview of Nearform and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.

Hiring Manager Interview (1 hour, Zoom)A conversation with the Head of Delivery or CTO focused on your approach to delivery management, client collaboration, and technical problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.

Panel Interview (1.5 hours, Zoom)
A discussion with 2 Technical Directors focusing on your team leadership and delivery management approach in more detail. This includes scenario-based questions on team management, delivering technical work, and client collaboration, assessing how you drive success in an enterprise development environment.

Final Interview (45 mins, Zoom)A final chat with the Managing Director for the region to discuss the plans for this role, Nearform’s strategy, and any questions you may have.

Ready to Join Us?

If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.


Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence.

If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.

Salary up to £150,000 + Bonus & Benefits

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Remote Project Manager to oversee the seamless deployment of low voltage technology systems and solutions, with a focus on specific deployments of CCTV, Network, WiFi, Fiber, and Data Lines. As a remote project manager, you will play a critical role in ensuring the successful implementation of these solutions for our clients located across various geographical locations.

Responsibilities:

  1. Project Planning: Collaborate with clients, stakeholders, and team members to gather project requirements, formulate project plans, and define project deliverables and timelines.

  2. Project Execution: Lead remote teams in the implementation and deployment of low voltage technology systems, including CCTV, Network, WiFi, Fiber, and Data Lines, ensuring adherence to project specifications, quality standards, and best practices.

  3. Resource Management: Allocate resources effectively, including remote contractors and subcontractors as necessary, to meet project milestones and timelines.

  4. Risk and Issue Management: Identify potential risks and issues, create mitigation strategies, and proactively resolve any challenges that may arise during the project lifecycle.

  5. Communication and Collaboration: Facilitate effective communication among stakeholders, team members, and clients through regular meetings, updates, and status reports.

  6. Documentation: Maintain accurate project documentation, including project plans, progress reports, change orders, and final deliverables.

  7. Project Budgeting and Cost Control: Monitor project expenses, track budget utilization, and ensure projects are delivered within budget constraints.

  8. Quality Assurance: Conduct regular project evaluations and quality checks to ensure all low voltage technology systems and solutions are implemented to meet client expectations.

  9. Technical Expertise: Stay up-to-date with industry trends, advancements, and emerging technologies related to low voltage technology systems, and provide technical guidance and expertise to clients and team members.


Requirements

  1. Proven experience (2 years) as a Project Manager in the low voltage technology systems industry, specifically with deployments of CCTV, Network, WiFi, Fiber, and Data Lines.

  2. Strong project management skills, including project planning, execution, resource allocation, risk management, and budget control.

  3. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with remote teams, clients, and stakeholders.

  4. Demonstrated ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously.

  5. In-depth knowledge of low voltage technology systems, industry standards, and best practices.

  6. Familiarity with project management software and tools for remote collaboration and communication.

  7. Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities, with a focus on finding practical solutions while considering project constraints.

  8. PMP or CAPM certification is a plus.

As a Remote Project Manager for Low Voltage Technology Systems and Solutions, you will have the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge projects, work with diverse teams, and play a crucial role in delivering high-quality solutions to our clients. If you are a detail-oriented, self-motivated professional with a passion for technology and project management, we would love to hear from you!

Note: This job description is meant to provide a general overview of the responsibilities and qualifications associated with the role of a Remote Project Manager for Low Voltage Technology Systems and Solutions. The specific tasks and requirements may vary depending on the organization and project requirements.

Include ability to bid potential projects using architectual plans

Additional Requirement: Ability to Bid Potential Projects Using Architectural Plans

In addition to the responsibilities mentioned in the job description for a Remote Project Manager for Low Voltage Technology Systems and Solutions, we also require the ability to bid potential projects using architectural plans. As part of this role, you will be responsible for reviewing architectural plans provided by clients and preparing accurate and competitive bids for low voltage technology system deployments.

Responsibilities (Specific to Bidding Process):

  1. Architectural Plan Review: Analyze architectural plans provided by clients to understand the scope, requirements, and specifications of the low voltage technology systems to be implemented.

  2. Cost Estimation: Prepare detailed cost estimates for materials, equipment, labor, and any other resources required for the project, ensuring accuracy and compliance with budget requirements.

  3. Supplier/Vendor Coordination: Collaborate with suppliers and vendors to obtain quotes and negotiate competitive pricing for materials and equipment needed for the project.

  4. Proposal Development: Create comprehensive project proposals that outline the scope of work, technical details, cost breakdowns, timelines, and any other pertinent information required for the bid.

  5. Competitive Analysis: Conduct research and analysis to ensure competitiveness in bidding, taking into account market trends, industry standards, and comparable projects.

  6. Bid Submission: Prepare and submit bids in a timely manner, adhering to client deadlines and procurement processes.

  7. Contract Negotiation: Participate in contract negotiations with clients to finalize project agreements, ensuring mutual understanding of expectations and deliverables.

Qualifications (Specific to Bidding Process):

  1. Experience in preparing bids for low voltage technology system deployments, using architectural plans as references.

  2. Strong understanding of architectural plans, including electrical and low voltage system drawings.

  3. Knowledge of low voltage technology system components, pricing, and industry standards for accurate cost estimation.

Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.

By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.

With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.

Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.

Stord’s software suite has expanded rapidly over the last year, and that’s only just the beginning. With a powerful fulfillment network, incredible reach, and top tier brands, we have an exciting opportunity ahead of us to transform a trillion dollar market. We are actively recruiting Product Managers across all our areas, whether that’s looking at our parcel network (TMS), helping optimize our fulfilment (WMS), thinking about automation and the future of AI (Stord Labs), or working with brands to increase customer LTV in Commerce, and more. Everything from customer-facing SaaS and OMS/WMS surfaces to the operational systems that move real inventory through real warehouses and onto real trucks.

This posting isn't tied to a single team; while Supply Chain and commerce knowledge is a huge plus, what matters most to us is how you operate. How you handle ambiguity, how quickly you turn a fuzzy problem into a shipped decision, and how well you partner with engineering in an AI-accelerated build environment. We’re looking for PMs who want to own a 0->1 product journey, who are excited by the challenge of transforming a fragmented industry into a compound network, and who are excited by the complexity that comes with Supply Chain, not put off by it.

As you go through the interview process, we’ll start to naturally align you with the product area that best fits your unique skills and interests, rather than locking you into a set path on day 1.

What You’ll Own:

  • Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for your product area, and make the explicit calls on what's in v1 versus what waits.

  • Talk directly to customers and internal stakeholders to find the real problem underneath the requested feature.

  • Turn ambiguous — sometimes physical-world — problems into clear concept docs, requirements, and acceptance criteria that engineering can build against.

  • Partner day-to-day with engineering and design, including AI-accelerated engineering workflows, to ship fast without breaking what's already running in production.

  • Define the metrics that tie your product to business outcomes — not just feature-shipped counts — and report on them without spin.

  • Represent your roadmap and tradeoffs to cross-functional and executive stakeholders clearly and concisely.

  • Get close enough to the operation your product supports — a warehouse floor, a carrier integration, a checkout flow — to know where your logic breaks before a customer tells you.

What You’ll Need:

  • 3-10+ years in product management, with a track record of owning a product area end-to-end — from discovery through launch and iteration.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguity: you've built the roadmap, not just executed someone else's.

  • Strong written and verbal communication — you can translate the same problem for engineers, operators, and executives without losing precision.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, AI-accelerated build environment, with a point of view on where AI genuinely helps product work and where it doesn't.

  • Analytical rigor: you use data and direct customer research to make prioritization calls, and you can defend a “no” as confidently as a “yes.”

  • A genuine curiosity about how physical operations work — you don't need supply chain experience on day one, but you need to want it by day thirty.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Exposure to logistics, supply chain, warehouse, or transportation systems (WMS, TMS, OMS, ERP) — a plus, not a prerequisite.

  • Experience at a product-led or product-forward organization (consumer or B2B SaaS, marketplace, fintech, etc.) where you learned rigorous product craft.

  • Experience building 0-to-1 products, or rebuilding/migrating a legacy platform.

  • Technical fluency strong enough to hold a real conversation with engineering about data models, APIs, or architecture tradeoffs.

What Success Looks Like (First 90 Days):

  • You've shipped or meaningfully progressed at least one roadmap item, backed by a clear, data-informed rationale.

  • Engineering and cross-functional partners describe you as someone who makes decisions, not just facilitates them.

  • You understand the operational reality behind your product area well enough to have an opinion on where it breaks.

Enterprise AI has shifted rapidly from experimentation to execution. Companies are investing in models, agents, AI platforms, data infrastructure, and AI-enabled applications, but many are struggling to translate those investments into production systems and measurable business outcomes.

The challenge is no longer simply selecting an AI model or platform. Enterprises must identify the right workflows, connect AI to their proprietary data and knowledge, integrate existing systems, build and deploy agents and applications, establish evaluation and control frameworks, drive adoption, and continuously operate and improve AI in production.

Toptal brings together world-class AI and domain talent, forward-deployed solution delivery, AI platforms and capabilities, strategic technology partners, expert-in-the-loop operations, and managed services to help enterprises move from AI promise to production.

This role exists to convert that market opportunity into new enterprise relationships and position Toptal as a strategic partner for companies deploying AI across their organizations.

This is a remote position with significant client-facing fieldwork across the US. Applicants who reside within commutable distance of a major metropolitan area are strongly preferred. We do not offer visa sponsorship or assistance. Applicants must be authorized to work in the US at the time of hire. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

You will be responsible for building a targeted portfolio of accounts via identifying, prioritizing, and developing your own book of business rather than inheriting an existing one. Once you have signed net new customers, you will partner with Client Partners to deepen and expand those strategic relationships over time.

Net new accounts may begin with a specific AI initiative, workflow, platform implementation, or business problem requiring a disciplined approach to defining the opportunity and matching the right Toptal capabilities to the client’s needs. As relationships mature, accounts become more complex, with deeper engagement across multiple business units, workflows, technology platforms, and senior executive relationships.

These accounts demand a highly consultative, strategic approach that includes navigating cross-functional priorities, understanding the client’s AI and technology environment, aligning solutions to evolving business objectives, and demonstrating credibility at the C-suite level. Success will require the ability to adapt your engagement style to the maturity and complexity of each account while consistently driving measurable client value and long-term growth.

  • Own and build a portfolio of enterprise AI accounts, with direct accountability for new logo acquisition, revenue growth, and client outcomes.
  • Prospect, pitch, negotiate, and close new opportunities in close partnership with our Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), while expanding the relationships you establish.
  • Define and execute account strategy, including opportunity creation, pipeline development, and multi-year growth planning.
  • Lead AI solution development and deal execution in partnership with AI Services leadership, Industry GMs, Practice Leaders, Pursuits, Partnerships, and Delivery teams.
  • Partner with Client Partners to drive coordinated account expansion and maximize total account value as accounts mature.
  • Shape AI solutions that apply Toptal’s capabilities across AI Strategy & Transformation, Agentic Solutions, Data Services, AI Platforms, Industry Solutions, Joint Partner Solutions, and Managed Services to clients’ most important business and operating challenges.
  • Maintain disciplined pipeline and account intelligence to support accurate forecasting and informed decision-making.
  • Lead strategic conversations with prospective and existing clients, while exercising discretion and independent judgment.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Familiarize yourself with the tools and resources needed to be successful.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Learn about the Toptal AI Go-To-Market Strategy, our key sales plays, solution portfolio, partner ecosystem, and client engagement model.
  • Work with AI Services leadership to establish a portfolio strategy and build account plans.
  • Shadow key calls and client meetings.
  • Begin to meet with clients, leveraging your existing enterprise AI network and relationships, to articulate Toptal’s capabilities and identify where we can help organizations move AI into production.
  • Begin prospecting and actively engaging target accounts within your portfolio.
  • Meet with SDRs, Client Partners, and cross-functional team members to align on joint account strategies.
  • Collaborate with Pursuits and Delivery teams to understand how we design AI engagements.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Exercise discretion and independent judgment in the negotiation of contracts, work collaboratively with clients, and help them engage with Toptal’s AI capabilities and specialists.
  • Begin shaping AI solutions that resonate with your target accounts, including forward-deployed AI solutions, Outcome Agents, agentic workflows, enterprise data and knowledge solutions, AI platforms, and managed AI services, demonstrating your comfort and ability in working with ambiguity and directly innovating alongside your clients.
  • Establish credibility with client stakeholders through informed, consultative engagement tied to their AI priorities, business workflows, existing technology investments, and desired outcomes.
  • Own your pipeline and forecast with confidence.
  • Develop proposals and close your first set of deals.
  • Actively contribute to team rituals, best practice sharing, and win/loss reviews.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Expand your buyer network and deepen executive engagement across your accounts.
  • Drive net new opportunities by introducing additional AI capabilities, platforms, solutions, partners, and managed services and displacing incumbent providers.
  • Shape and influence client priorities, aligning Toptal’s AI solutions to critical business objectives and measurable, validated outcomes.
  • Execute against a defined growth plan tied to measurable outcomes.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Have built a list of incredible client accounts, advising them on how to utilize Toptal’s AI capabilities to address their priorities and key business challenges.
  • Establish and expand a strong executive network across your portfolio, building a foundation of advocates and sponsors.
  • Begin to mentor new members of the team, teaching them about Toptal, our AI model, and how to successfully grow their territory.

  • Direct experience selling enterprise AI solutions is required, ideally including forward-deployed AI solutions, AI software or platforms, AI consulting and professional services, or managed AI services.

  • Must be comfortable engaging C-level executives on how AI is changing their business, technology environment, operating model, workforce, and competitive landscape.
  • A well-rounded understanding of enterprise AI challenges and trends, including generative AI, agentic AI, AI applications and platforms, enterprise data and knowledge, models, workflow automation, governance, evaluation, controls, and managed AI operations.
  • Ability to have informed discussions about how AI moves from strategy and experimentation into real enterprise workflows and production environments, including the importance of context, data, integration, validation, governance, adoption, and ongoing operations.
  • Experience selling solutions involving leading AI, cloud, data, or enterprise technology platforms, and the ability to work in a platform-flexible environment across client technology ecosystems.
  • Exposure to hybrid talent models, forward-deployed delivery models, or alternative consulting delivery models.
  • Ability to build and execute account plans that lead to consistent portfolio growth and a healthy pipeline.

  • Ability to partner effectively across multiple internal teams to shape innovative solutions that drive client success.

  • Passion for solving client problems with creativity and urgency.
  • Regular or periodic travel to meet and engage with Toptal clients and customers both inside and outside of your geographic location.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
