jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.excerpt: Edurio is on its way to improving education quality globally and we're looking for great people to join us on the journey.
jobs.description:
Edurio is on its way to improving education quality globally and we're looking for great people to join us on the journey.

We help schools and school groups survey their parents, pupils, and staff to build organisations where people thrive. We currently work with over 2000 schools in the United Kingdom and Latvia and are planning to grow significantly in the next year.

As an Engineering Manager, you will lead our development team and own what it commits to. You will also own how the team works, so that a new developer can learn it in their first week.

The development team and how we work

You would lead our development team, five people today and growing: four developers and a QA engineer. Product is a separate team of four, led by our Lead Product Manager.

Our Principal Engineer works alongside you and owns the architecture, the database schema, the technologies we build on, and what our development standard says. You own the people, the commitments, the process, and whether the standard is followed in the work that ships. Neither of you reports to the other, and you both report to the Director of Product and Service.

This role is being created as part of the restructure that comes with becoming a multi-product company.

Our developers direct coding agents and verify what comes back, so most of an engineer's day is design and review rather than manually writing code.

We run two products on one platform: the survey software, and Edurio Hub, the second product we are building now. The platform is mid-migration, so we are reducing the PHP monolith, moving the front end to Vue 3, and building new services on AWS with CDK.

You would be working with Vue and TypeScript, AWS Lambda and CDK, and with Linear, Slack, Claude, and other tools of your choice.

Your responsibilities

  • Lead the developers and the QA engineer: expectations and performance, growth, workload and wellbeing, keeping people here, and hiring future engineers

  • Actively participate in writing code yourself - we are looking for a player-coach rather than a manager who is removed from coding

  • Own the team’s commitments, release planning and adjusting the plan when something unexpected happens

  • Own how we estimate work and ensure the accuracy and consistency of estimates given by the development team

  • Run the rhythm the team works to: standups, planning, demos and retrospectives

  • Ensure that the team follows our development standards and highlight situations where our standards do not match current practice

  • Own how development and product work together, from the kick-off to a release the product team can explain to clients

  • Explain the technical side to the rest of the company: what an incident means, what a security questionnaire is asking for, and what a constraint will cost

What we're looking for

  • Experience of leading in an engineering team that builds with coding agents

  • Ability to handle the people side: holding the team accountable, ensuring the team’s wellbeing and leading growth planning and performance conversations.

  • Enough seniority h in engineering to coordinate the team’s work, although we don’t expect you to be the most experienced engineer in the room

  • Experience putting a development process in place and teaching it, rather than running one you inherited

  • Ability to explain delivery, risk and trade-offs to people who do not write software

  • Advanced use of AI and coding agents in your own work

  • Excellent verbal and written English skills

Useful, but we do not expect all of these:

  • Experience with Typescript, Vue or AWS serverless

  • Experience of a platform migration that ran alongside feature work

  • Experience or interest in the EdTech sector

This is probably not for you if:

  • You want to fully own the architecture and the technology choices

  • You want to code full time and leave the people side to somebody else

  • You want to join a team whose process is already settled

The attitudes we'd like to see

Ownership: You do what you said you would do, and take responsibility for how it lands with the client - not just for completing the task

Genuine care: You build real relationships with clients and colleagues, assume good intentions, and do the right thing rather than the easy thing

Openness: You communicate honestly, don't shy away from difficult conversations, and give and receive feedback well

Growth: You're curious about how things could work better, and you act on what you learn rather than defaulting to how it's always been done

What we offer

Experience in growing in an international company and a chance to have an impact on education quality

Feedback-based work culture which highly values transparency and team well-being

Flexible working hours. For colleagues based in Latvia we offer a hybrid setup with an office in Riga. The UK-based colleagues are fully remote.

Gross salary from EUR 5000 per month in Latvia or GBP 60,000 per annum in the UK, as well as company share options, paid phone plan, and health insurance.

Novakid is on a mission to build the best online education platform for kids worldwide. We've already got over 90,000 students and 3,500 teachers making learning awesome in over 30 countries in Europe and Asia. But we're not stopping there—we need your help to take things to the next level!

We're searching for a senior backend developer who's brilliant with Python, PostgreSQL, and REST APIs, and who's also got a solid understanding of cutting-edge AI models. You'll be joining a small, super-effective team focused on developing the AI magic that powers our language learning platform.

What we offer

Fully remote work (core hours GMT+3).

A chance to shape the future of AI-driven education.

A fun, dynamic team that loves building innovative products.

Unlimited holidays – because we trust you to deliver.

Bonuses and stock options – we grow together.

Requirements

What you'll bring

A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or something similar.

5+ years of hands-on experience as a Python Developer. You should be comfortable working with Python 3.8+

Deep experience in designing and building scalable backends and REST APIs. Our stack includes PostgreSQL, Redis, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Celery, and pydantic.

A strong grasp of modern LLMs (like OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), agentic tools (like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Amp) and real experience building solutions that use them.

AI-Native Engineering Workflow

Hands-on experience with AI coding agents in CLI environments: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Amp, or similar tools for backend development. You should understand how to orchestrate multi-step engineering tasks—breaking down complex features into agent-executable chunks, reviewing AI-generated code critically, and maintaining architectural integrity. Familiarity with plan-execute-review workflows where AI agents propose implementation strategies before coding. Understanding of compound AI systems—not just using LLMs, but orchestrating multiple AI tools in your development workflow.

Proficiency in context engineering for team collaboration: setting up and maintaining shared configuration files (agents.md, CLAUDE.md, custom skills/plugins) that encode team conventions, API patterns, and deployment practices. Experience sharing these configurations across teams to ensure consistent AI-assisted development. Understanding of compound AI systems—not just using LLMs, but orchestrating multiple AI tools in your development workflow.

Experience with microservice architecture and the AWS serverless stack.

You should be fluent in English.

Bonus points if

You've worked in startups or small teams.

You're a self-starter who also thrives as part of a team.

You're all about solving business problems, not just writing code.

You can use AI tools to create solutions quickly, in days or hours, not weeks or months.

You have experience with e-commerce or e-learning projects.

You've led teams or mentored other developers.

You've deployed applications on AWS.

You know your stuff when it comes to modern software architecture.

You've worked with no/low-code workflow automation.

jobs.title: Principal Solutions Architect - Quantum-Safe Networks
jobs.excerpt: About IonQ: IonQ, Inc.  [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security.
jobs.description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Location: This position is US-based and can work onsite or hybrid from one of our offices or fully remote.
Travel: Up to 30%, domestic and international
Job ID: 1779

The Role:

We are looking for a Principal Solutions Architect to design how networks become quantum-safe — for the largest network operators, enterprises, and government agencies in the world.

Today's networks are secured with cryptography that a cryptographically relevant quantum computer will break. Every operator and enterprise will have to inventory their cryptography, make it agile, migrate to post-quantum algorithms, and in the highest-assurance segments complement that with quantum-safe key distribution. Almost nobody knows yet what that architecture actually looks like. That is the problem you will solve — first with customers, on real networks, and then as reusable architectures that shape what IonQ builds.

This role sits deliberately in multiple places. A part of your time is customer-facing: in collaboration with our GTM colleagues, you'll lead architecture discussions, design quantum-safe target architectures and migration paths, run proofs of concept and interoperability tests, and support complex pursuits as the technical authority. The other part of your time is spent on design authority, standards work, and providing thought leadership internally and externally, including public speaking: turning what you learn in the field from internal and external peers into reference architectures, migration playbooks, standards, white papers, blogs, conference talks, and product requirements that our engineering and product teams build against.

You are equally comfortable in a firewall design review as you are in a discussion about hybrid key exchange and crypto-agility. You can explain to a CISO why their crypto inventory is the hard part, and to a network engineer exactly which IPsec algorithms to use and where they could insert external key material in order to become quantum-safe.

This is not a software architecture role — you will not own a codebase (it’s a plus if you can do some scripting). It is an architecture and customer role: you own designs, decisions, and the technical credibility of IonQ's quantum-safe networking story.

Responsibilities:

  • Design quantum-safe target architectures and migration paths for customer networks — spanning WAN and transport, data center and campus, segmentation and access control, key management, and the crypto that underpins all of it.
  • Lead technical discovery and architecture workshops with network, security, and infrastructure teams. Assess the current state, identify where cryptography is embedded and where it is brittle, and build a migration plan the customer can actually execute.
  • Own the technical thread in complex pursuits: architecture proposals, RFI/RFP responses, security and compliance questions, competitive positioning, and objection handling — in partnership with Sales.
  • In collaboration with the Sales Engineers, design and run proofs of concept, interoperability tests, and pilots — including PQC and hybrid key exchange in production-representative network environments and, where relevant, QKD-integrated links — together with our engineering teams and customer staff.
  • Translate field learning into reusable reference architectures, migration playbooks, interoperability matrices, and design guides that scale beyond the deals you personally work.
  • Serve as the customer's voice in the product process. Bring architectural constraints, integration gaps, and roadmap requirements to Product and Engineering with enough specificity to be actionable, and hold us to them.
  • Track how the standards and threat landscape actually move and contribute to them — NIST PQC standards and migration guidance, protocol work in the IETF, national and sector-specific mandates and deadlines — and keep our architectures and guidance ahead of it.
  • Partner with Marketing, Corporate Communications, and GTM to build IonQ's technical presence in the networking and security community: talks, papers, blogs, standards bodies, and industry events.
  • Raise the technical bar around you — architecture reviews, mentoring, and the design patterns the rest of the team reuses.

Requirements:

  • 15+ years designing and securing enterprise and/or service provider networks, in a solutions architecture, network architecture, security architecture, or senior customer-facing engineering capacity.
  • Deep (hands-on) knowledge of how networks are built and secured today: routing and switching, IP transport, network segmentation, firewall and access control design, VPN and encryption at the network layer, and Zero Trust principles applied to real infrastructure. Multi-vendor experience (for example, Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Nokia) is expected.
  • Working knowledge of applied cryptography as it appears in networks: TLS, IPsec, MACsec, PKI and certificate lifecycle, key management, and how algorithm and key material choices are made and changed in practice.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in front of customers at multiple levels — leading workshops, running architecture discussions with engineers, and holding a credible conversation with a CISO or SVP of Infrastructure about risk, cost, and sequencing.
  • A serious interest in where this is heading, and enough grounding to be credible on day one: post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility, quantum key distribution, and the migration challenge facing existing networks. You do not need to have shipped a PQC migration — very few people have — but you should be able to reason about the problem rigorously and be visibly motivated to go deep.
  • Strong written communication. Architectures, migration plans, and design guidance are a large part of the output.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Willingness to travel up to 30%, primarily within the US, with incidental international travel.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with post-quantum cryptography migration: cryptographic discovery and inventory, crypto-agility architecture, hybrid key exchange, or PQC deployment in a network or PKI context.
  • Hands-on exposure to quantum key distribution or quantum networking — testbeds, carrier or research trials, key delivery interfaces to encryptors, or optical and transport-layer integration.
  • Experience at a network or security vendor, service provider, hyperscaler, or a large enterprise network or security team — with real accountability for architecture decisions at scale.
  • Familiarity with the security and compliance frameworks customers will map this work to: NIST CSF, CIS Benchmarks, ISO 27001, FISMA, FedRAMP, or sector-specific regulation.
  • Public-sector, defense, financial services, or telecom experience, where high-assurance and long data-confidentiality horizons make this problem urgent today.
  • Contributions to standards or the technical community: IETF, ETSI, national PQC migration working groups, published writing, or conference talks.
  • Certifications that validate technical depth — CISSP, CCIE/JNCIE, CCNP Security, or equivalent.
  • Comfort with automation and tooling — Python, config-as-code, network telemetry — enough to build a credible demo or analysis yourself rather than waiting on someone else.

jobs.description:
At Anchorage Digital, we are building the world’s most advanced digital asset platform for institutions to participate in crypto.
Anchorage Digital is a crypto platform that enables institutions to participate in digital assets through custody, staking, trading, governance, settlement, and the industry's leading security infrastructure. Home to Anchorage Digital Bank N.A., the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., Anchorage Digital also serves institutions through Anchorage Digital Singapore, Porto by Anchorage Digital, and other offerings.
The company is funded by leading institutions including Andreessen Horowitz, GIC, Goldman Sachs, KKR, and Visa, with its Series D valuation over $3 billion. Founded in 2017 in San Francisco, California, Anchorage Digital has offices in New York, New York; Porto, Portugal; Singapore; and Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Learn more at anchorage.com, on X @Anchorage, and on LinkedIn.

With the evolving landscape of digital threats and an increasing volume of sophisticated attacks by malicious actors, we have a security policy mandating all new hires complete an in-person onboarding process - no exceptions. Security is our foundation and we prioritize physical identity verification and secure IT setup. While our security and IT logistics require physical presence to protect our infrastructure from sophisticated global threats, this move is equally about our Village culture. We believe that a laptop can be shipped, but our culture cannot.

  • As a Trader on the Trading Solutions team, you have the unique opportunity to contribute to the growth of the trading business at Anchorage Digital. You will be responsible for facilitating the hedging needs of client flows, ensuring that we provide clients with best in class service, while also managing our risk exposures well within the constraints of the company risk appetite. Being fully successful in this role requires responsiveness and attention to detail during all client and market interactions, while also improving the trading offering through tooling and technical investments. We are investing heavily into our trading technology, and your front-line input will be valuable in prioritizing product features to grow our market share.
  • We have created the Factors of Growth & Impact to help Villagers better measure impact and articulate coaching, feedback, and the rich and rewarding learning that happens while exploring, developing, and mastering the capabilities and contributions within and outside of the OTC Trading role:

Technical Skills:

  • Ability to expertly handle complex trades with a mindset of continuous optimization. Every basis point of execution is significant and should be measured and understood, with the goal of increasing the trading desk’s revenue while abiding by risk management guardrails.
  • Deep crypto market microstructure expertise with ability to identify profitable price gaps while protecting our assets from market volatility and aggressive automated traders, staying one step ahead of market trends.
  • Demonstrates expert knowledge of both electronic and voice trading, influencing technology improvements inspired by the more mature Traditional Finance market structure.
  • Strong client-facing abilities, instilling confidence through excellent white glove service; influencing clients to increase Anchorage’s share of wallet.
  • Traders on the desk use Python to automate manual tasks until the Engineering or Data Science teams deploy more robust solutioning. While Python expertise is not a requirement, you should be comfortable using Python code as needed, and over time develop proficiency in modifying existing code to fit the evolving needs of the desk.

Complexity and Impact of Work:

  • Perform principal trading exposure management infrastructure and processes. This includes building and optimizing the trading desk’s pricing, risk models and governing controls.
  • Contribute to efforts of increasing automation, so that traders can focus on only the most complicated trades, project work, or client engagement.
  • Closely follow market narratives to contribute perspectives to internal research efforts, which may be used to increase engagement with trading clients.
  • Help to inform new products and capabilities within the trading business to meet our clients’ overall needs
  • While on coverage, be available to immediately respond to changing exposures, client questions and requests. This includes rotations on weekends and off-hours.

Organizational Knowledge:

  • Is keenly aware of how Trading fits within the firm’s broader strategy, both as a tool and a standalone business, to provide input to the technology roadmap and implementation.
  • Understands upstream and downstream implications of process changes, proactively voicing ideas and concerns as the business scales. This includes understanding industry trends, regulatory guidelines, and best practices related to trading and settlements.
  • Ensures that knowledge is shared among stakeholder teams and does not position themselves or others as a single point of failure.

Communication and Influence:

  • Stay up to date with the underlying themes driving market prices and liquidity to deepen client interactions and execution strategies.
  • Champion the perspective of the Trading Solutions team during cross-department conversations and with existing clients.
  • Act as a mentor for more junior members of the team, empowering the team to become experts in our current processes, while collaborating to implement enhancements to the trading desk

You may be a fit for this role if you have:

  • 3+ years experience as an OTC trader in the cryptocurrency space.
  • Demonstrated ability to convert institutional prospects into trading clients.

Although not a requirement, bonus points if:

  • You’re proud of your crypto Twitter feed and ability to uncover narratives driving crypto markets and specific coins.
  • You enjoy using memes as a method of communication.
  • You were emotionally moved by the soundtrack to Hamilton, which chronicles the founding of a new financial system. :)

The Anchorage Village, what we call our team, brings together the brightest minds from platform security, financial services, and distributed ledger technology to provide the building blocks that empower institutions to safely participate in the evolving digital asset ecosystem. As a diverse team of more than 600 members, we are united in one common goal: building the future of finance by providing the foundation upon which value moves safely in the new global economy.
Anchorage Digital is committed to being a welcoming and inclusive workplace for everyone, and we are intentional about making sure people feel respected, supported, and connected at work—regardless of who you are or where you come from. We value and celebrate our differences and we believe being open about who we are allows us to do the best work of our lives.

  • Oversee and validate statistical programming deliverables to ensure analyses are accurate, reproducible and aligned with study objectives, regulatory and publication standards.
  • Perform statistical programming using relevant programming languages in big data environment to support data extraction, analysis, validation and generation of study results.
  • Apply AI capabilities to enhance data preparation, code development, analytical efficiency and workflow automation.

Responsibilities:

  • Develops individual protocol/SAP and determines appropriate statistical methodology for RWD/RWE studies.
